Positions created before the DAO fee launch (2026-07-19; enabled 2026-07-21 on BNB Chain and Robinhood Chain) carry no DAO fee and contribute only to SupplySideRevenue. Cross-checked against measured ERC20 inflows to the fee exchangers.

methodology.Fees: The fee a V5 or V6 launch pool charges on each trade, taken by that launch's hook inside the swap itself and read from the hook's own event, so the rate is never assumed here. It is 1% at regime; an anti-sniper launch charges more on buys during its opening window, on a curve that decays over the first blocks - 95%, then 70%, 40% and 10% - before settling at the same 1%, while sells in that window pay the regime rate. The fee is taken in either the launched token or its quote asset, whichever side the trader paid in. Both generations are read: V6 only took over new launches, it did not stop V5's existing pools from trading. V1-V4 legacy launches (pre-hook, plain Uniswap v3 with a per-launch lock contract) are not covered.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Everything not kept by the protocol: the creator's share, the remainder streamed to the launched token's own holders via the Reward Vault on Holder-Rewards launches, and - on fees taken during the opening window - the 80% earmarked to the launch's Treasury Reserve, which buys the launched token back to burn it.

methodology.Fees: The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.
methodology.Revenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.

Fees.Swap Tax: The launch's own buy and sell tax, chosen per launch (1-10%), taken by its hook on each swap: on Portals 3-7 read from that swap's TaxTaken, net of the tax the splitter pays itself when it sells launched tokens through the launch's own pool, which is not paid by any user; on Portal 8 the tax part of QuoteFeeTaken's bucketFee. The hook charges it outside the pool fee, so it is not inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc.
Fees.LP Fees: Portals 3-7: the 1% Uniswap v4 pool fee earned by the launch's permanently locked position, read as what the locker forwarded to the splitter, net of the position principal that comes back through the same call. These fees are also inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: Portal 8: the 1% base fee the hook adds to every buy and sell and takes in the quote asset. Portal 8 pools are dynamic-fee pools whose pool fee is set to zero on every swap, so this replaces the LP fee and goes to the same split; it is not inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc. It is the base's proportional part of QuoteFeeTaken's bucketFee, which prices tax and base as one rate.
Fees.Snipe Tax: An extra, time-decaying tax on buys in the seconds after a launch opens, charged by the same hook and paid directly to the treasury (Portal 8: QuoteFeeTaken's surcharge).

Revenue.Swap Fees to Treasury: treasuryBps of each launch's accrued fee, read from that launch's own splitter or escrow (1000 on every Portal 3-7 launch, 3000 on every Portal 8 launch), plus the whole snipe tax, which the hook pays straight to the treasury without passing through a splitter, plus on Portal 8 any holders' share accrued while no holder was eligible, which the hook also pays straight to the treasury.

methodology.Fees: What users pay to cross the bridge. The asset's controller on Arc charges the same rate in both directions - on the way in it mints the fee to the protocol and the rest to the user, on the way out it burns the gross and re-mints the fee - and an optional fast-lane router charges its own cut on top for skipping the queue, on the origin chain when depositing and on Arc when redeeming. Anything charged on Arc is taken in the claim token (bCRCL, bGLD, bUSDT, bBTCB), which is a 1:1 claim on the asset held in custody and is therefore valued as that origin asset; a fast-lane deposit is charged on the origin chain instead, before the asset becomes a claim, so it is taken in the origin token directly. Either way the fee is denominated in the same four origin assets.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: what the trader paid on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Two things the trader pays. The pool fee on each swap - two of these pools run Ellipse's market-hours hook and charge 1%, 2% or 3% depending on whether the underlying market is open or shut, so for those the rate is read from the swap itself rather than assumed, and the rest are fixed at creation. Plus Ellipse's own 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, read from the event its fee collector emits when it is emptied, which reports what actually reached the treasury rather than what was sent.
methodology.Revenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.

methodology.Volume: Swap volume in Ellipse's own markets on Arc: the Uniswap pools it opened for the assets it bridges (bCRCL, bGLD, bBTCB, bUSDT) and the market for its own token. Each swap is counted once, on whichever side has a price - USDC everywhere except the ELLIPSE market, which is counted on its bCRCL side and valued as the CRCL held in custody behind it. Launchpad launches are not counted: those pools are opened for other people's tokens on Uniswap's shared PoolManager, so their volume belongs to that DEX.

methodology.Fees: The full native-USDC entry price accepted for every BoneYard NFT mint, read from Boneyard's Minted.price event. Excludes BONE genesis reserve, BONE emitted by burns, secondary royalties, and hook swap levies.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every included amount is paid by a miner in a successful Boneyard mint.
methodology.Revenue: Mint fees less Charge paid to existing Skeletons. Before LP activation, the retained revenue is the project share plus protocol-owned liquidity bootstrap; after LP activation it is the project share plus BONE-buyback funding.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Charge accrued to active Skeleton holders from mint #9 onward (65% under the deployed constant). Charge is measured when it accrues, not when a holder later claims or burns.

If seedLiquidity diverts bootstrap that cannot be paired with BONE into the Hook buyback reserve, that previously booked protocol revenue is reclassified out on BootstrapDivertedToBuyback. Hook-bound revenue is 100% of each of the first eight genesis mints and 35% of later mints.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Native USDC allocated by Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded from post-LP mints for market-buying and burning BONE, plus any pre-LP bootstrap reclassified to that reserve by BootstrapDivertedToBuyback at liquidity seeding. It is counted when funded, not when the owner executes the capped buyback. BONE is the protocol's own value-accrual token.

Fees.Boneyard Mint Fees: The exact price field from each successful Boneyard Minted event.

Revenue.Mint Fees To Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bo: Pre-LP mint share retained by Boneyard and later committed to its canonical protocol-owned liquidity position.
Revenue.BONE Buyback Reserve: Post-LP mint share credited to the BONE buyback-and-burn reserve.

ProtocolRevenue.Mint Rounding Remainder Retained In Bone: Native wei retained by Boneyard from Solidity's independent integer floors for Charge and the hook share.

HoldersRevenue.BONE Buyback Reserve: Post-LP mint funding for BONE market buybacks and burns, read from Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded and excluding seed-time bootstrap diversion.
HoldersRevenue.Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bootstrap Recla: Bootstrap previously classified as protocol-owned liquidity that seedLiquidity explicitly diverts to the BONE buyback-and-burn reserve.

methodology.Fees: Actual quote-asset swap charges emitted by the verified TaxHook FeesAccrued event. V1 launches charge no trading tax. No token mint allocation, gas, deposits, claim payments or buyback execution is counted as a new fee.
methodology.Revenue: Treasury allocation of each fee on an accrual basis; excludes creators, referrers and launched-token buybacks.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The same treasury allocation as Revenue. Fledgo has no own-token holder revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator recipients, attributed referrers and launched-token buyback allocations. Missing referrers retain their allocation for creators. Buybacks benefit the launched token, not a Fledgo governance token.

Fees.Trading fees: Exact totalFee in FeesAccrued, denominated in that registered pool configuration quote asset. Native ETH and native Arc USDC are 18-decimal raw amounts; ERC-20 quotes retain their own decimals. USD totals depend on DefiLlama historical price coverage.

Revenue.Trading fees to treasury: The immutable 40-bps protocol charge plus integer rounding dust, equal to the emitted total fee minus the gross quote amount times creatorBps floored per swap.

ProtocolRevenue.Trading fees to treasury: The immutable 40-bps protocol charge plus integer rounding dust, equal to the emitted total fee minus the gross quote amount times creatorBps floored per swap.

SupplySideRevenue.Trading fees to creator recipients: Per-swap gross quote times immutable creatorBps, minus buyback allocation and referral allocation only when the event names a nonzero referrer.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading fees to referrers: Per-swap gross quote times referralBps floored, only for an authenticated nonzero FeesAccrued referrer. Later claims are excluded.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading fees to launched-token buybacks: Per-swap gross quote times buybackBps floored; later buybacks and burns settle this allocation and are not new fees or protocol-holder revenue.

methodology.Fees: Everything PeddleQuest charges: the fee quest creators pay on top of the reward pool they deposit, the flat quest creation fee, the protocol's share of rewards that winners did not claim before the deadline, payments for trending and banner promotion slots, and the fee users pay to mint an optional completion badge.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: all of it is paid by quest creators, advertisers and badge minters. Joining a quest and claiming a reward are free.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (quest creation, deposit, unclaimed, promotion and badge) are kept by the protocol. Quest rewards themselves go to winners and are not counted as fees or revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Fees (quest creation, deposit, unclaimed, promotion and badge) accrued to the protocol treasury (a Safe multisig).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of badge mint fees routed on-chain to buyback and burn. Zero while that route is switched off, which it has been since launch.

Fees.Reward Pool Deposit Fees: Percentage fee (3% at launch, hard-capped at 10%) charged on top of each reward pool when a quest creator deposits it into escrow.
Fees.Quest Creation Fees: Flat fee per quest paid by the creator in the chain's gas token (free at launch).
Fees.Unclaimed Rewards Share: The protocol's share (20% at launch, hard-capped at 50%) of rewards winners left unclaimed after the claim deadline; the rest returns to the quest creator.
Fees.Promotion Slot Fees: Payments by advertisers for trending and banner slots, priced per day in the chain's gas token.
Fees.Badge Mint Fees: Fee paid by a user who chooses to mint the optional soulbound badge for a quest they completed.

Revenue.Quest Creation Fees To Treasury: Sent to the protocol treasury. Flat fee per quest paid by the creator in the chain's gas token (free at launch).
Revenue.Unclaimed Rewards Share To Treasury: Sent to the protocol treasury. The protocol's share (20% at launch, hard-capped at 50%) of rewards winners left unclaimed after the claim deadline; the rest returns to the quest creator.

ProtocolRevenue.Quest Creation Fees To Treasury: Sent to the protocol treasury. Flat fee per quest paid by the creator in the chain's gas token (free at launch).
ProtocolRevenue.Unclaimed Rewards Share To Treasury: Sent to the protocol treasury. The protocol's share (20% at launch, hard-capped at 50%) of rewards winners left unclaimed after the claim deadline; the rest returns to the quest creator.
ProtocolRevenue.Promotion Slot Fees To Treasury: Sent to the protocol treasury. Payments by advertisers for trending and banner slots, priced per day in the chain's gas token.
ProtocolRevenue.Badge Mint Fees To Treasury: Sent to the protocol treasury. Fee paid by a user who chooses to mint the optional soulbound badge for a quest they completed.

methodology.Fees: Platform fees, integrator app fees and swap costs paid by users on Relay bridges and swaps, excluding execution costs (network gas).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: App fees paid to the integrators that add them, and swap costs paid to liquidity providers. Excludes the integrator revenue share of the platform fee, which Relay does not disclose.
methodology.Revenue: Platform fees. This is an upper bound: Relay pays qualifying integrators an undisclosed 0-67% revenue share out of it.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Platform fees kept by Relay. This is an upper bound: Relay pays qualifying integrators an undisclosed 0-67% revenue share out of it.

Fees.Swap Costs: Payments to liquidity providers for cross-asset and cross-chain swaps. Excludes trades with unreliable token prices.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Costs To Liquidity Providers: Swap costs paid to the liquidity providers that fill cross-asset and cross-chain swaps.

SupplySideRevenue.Platform Fee Revenue Share To Integrator: Relay pays qualifying integrators a revenue share of 0-67% of its platform fee, depending on the swap type and their 30-day volume. Relay does not report the amount, so it cannot be measured.

methodology.Volume: One side of every trade made through Ryntra. On Solana, from the trader's own token movements in the trade: the stablecoin they paid or received, else the SOL, else the token they paid — gross of Ryntra's fee (a fee taken from what they received is added back). On Arc, from the swap's own events: the side in USDC, EURC, WETH or cirBTC of a KyberSwap swap, gross of the router's fees (the amount the fee was taken from), and the input a trader sent Circle's swap Adapter. A trade is Ryntra's when it paid Ryntra's fee inside it. Trades on the bonding curve of a token launched with Ryntra are counted under Ryntra Launch. Double counted: the venues the trades are routed through already list this volume.
methodology.Fees: Fees people pay Ryntra on trades made through it. On Solana: what the swap router (Jupiter, or DFlow when Jupiter routes through it) pays into Ryntra's fee wallet and its Jupiter referral account inside the trade. On Arc: the developer fee of a Circle swap and the fee leg of a KyberSwap swap that name Ryntra's fee address, read from Circle's fee collector and KyberSwap's router events. Plain transfers into these accounts are not fees.
methodology.UserFees: Fees traders pay Ryntra inside the trades they make through it.
methodology.Revenue: Trading fees kept by Ryntra: the whole fee paid into its fee wallet on Solana and from KyberSwap on Arc, what reached its Jupiter referral account less Jupiter's 20% share, and the Circle developer fee less the share (about 10%) Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient. Cashback and invite rewards are paid later, when people claim them, and are not deducted.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Trading fees kept by Ryntra, all of it for the protocol: Ryntra has no token and distributes nothing to holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Jupiter's 20% share of the fees that reached Ryntra's Jupiter referral account, and the share (about 10%) of the Circle developer fee that Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient on Arc.

Fees.Trading Fees: Ryntra's fee on swaps and spot trades, paid into its fee wallet or its Jupiter referral account on Solana, or to its fee address on Arc, inside the trade.

UserFees.Trading Fees: Ryntra's fee on swaps and spot trades, paid by the trader inside the trade.

Revenue.Trading Fees To Ryntra: The whole fee paid into the fee wallet and from KyberSwap, 80% of what reached the Jupiter referral account, and what the Circle developer fee leaves Ryntra after the protocol share (about 90%).

ProtocolRevenue.Trading Fees To Ryntra: The whole fee paid into the fee wallet and from KyberSwap, 80% of what reached the Jupiter referral account, and what the Circle developer fee leaves Ryntra after the protocol share (about 90%).

SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees To Jupiter: Jupiter's 20% share of the fees that reached Ryntra's Jupiter referral account.
SupplySideRevenue.Developer Fee Protocol Share: The share (about 10%) of the developer fee on a Circle swap that Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient on Arc, read from the collector's event.

methodology.Fees: The 1% bonding curve trading fee on every Ferzan coin before it graduates (Meteora's DBC fee on Solana, including Meteora's protocol share).
methodology.UserFees: The 1% fee paid by traders on every Ferzan coin before it graduates.
methodology.Revenue: Ferzan's share of the curve fee: 50%, less 10% to a referrer when one is set. On Solana, half of the DBC trading fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Ferzan's share of the curve fee: 50%, less 10% to a referrer when one is set. On Solana, half of the DBC trading fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The coin creator's 50%, referrer payouts, and on Solana Meteora's protocol fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: None.

Fees.Bonding Curve Trading Fees: 1% fee on every bonding curve buy and sell.
Fees.Meteora Protocol Fees: Meteora's protocol fee on Ferzan's Solana curves.

UserFees.Bonding Curve Trading Fees: 1% fee on every bonding curve buy and sell.
UserFees.Meteora Protocol Fees: Meteora's protocol fee on Ferzan's Solana curves.

Revenue.Bonding Curve Fees To Ferzan: Ferzan's share of the curve fee.

ProtocolRevenue.Bonding Curve Fees To Ferzan: Ferzan's share of the curve fee.

SupplySideRevenue.Bonding Curve Fees To Creators: Half of the curve fee, paid to the coin creator.
SupplySideRevenue.Bonding Curve Fees To Referrers: 10% of the curve fee, paid to the referrer of the trade when there is one.
SupplySideRevenue.Meteora Protocol Fees: Meteora's protocol fee on Solana curves.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders, plus bribes paid to the protocol to attract AERO Rewards to pools.
methodology.Revenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.

methodology.Volume: Swap volume on Aero volatile and stable pools.

Fees.External Bribes Rewards: Bribes (Aero calls them Liquidity Payments) paid to the protocol for a pool, counted as the protocol streams them out.

Revenue.Swap Fees To sAERO Holders: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity, distributed to sAERO holders.
Revenue.External Bribes Revenue: Bribes paid to the protocol, distributed to sAERO holders allocating to the pool.

HoldersRevenue.Swap Fees To sAERO Holders: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity, distributed to sAERO holders.
HoldersRevenue.External Bribes Revenue: Bribes paid to the protocol, distributed to sAERO holders allocating to the pool.

SupplySideRevenue.LP Fees: Swap fees kept by fee-earning liquidity providers.

methodology.Fees: EVM chains: swap fees of the pools sasa creates for every coin, counted when sasa's builder collects them: the quote-asset side (ETH, BNB or USDC) and the coin side (in the launched coin, valued where the coin has a price). Solana: the creator fees of coins launched on sasa (both halves).
methodology.UserFees: Traders pay the pool's swap fee (EVM) or the launch curve's creator fee (Solana) on every buy and sell.
methodology.Revenue: EVM: 70% of the collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault. Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: EVM: 70% of the collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault. Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: EVM: 30% of the collected swap fees, sent to each coin's creator, or used to buy back and burn the coin when its creator chose buybacks. Solana: the creators' 50% of the creator fees.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees of sasa-created Uniswap V4 / PancakeSwap Infinity pools, both sides, as collected by the builder (FeesCollected).
Fees.Creator Fees: Solana: creator fees of coins launched on sasa, shared 50/50 between sasa and the coin's creator.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees traders pay on every buy and sell in sasa-created pools.
UserFees.Creator Fees: Solana: the creator fee traders pay on every buy and sell of a coin launched on sasa.

Revenue.Swap Fees to sasa: 70% of collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault.
Revenue.Creator Fees to sasa: Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees to sasa: 70% of collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault.
ProtocolRevenue.Creator Fees to sasa: Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees to Creators and Buybacks: 30% of collected swap fees, sent to the coin's creator or used for its buy-and-burn.
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees to Creators: Solana: the creators' 50% of the creator fees.

methodology.Fees: Every swap in a Phlece coin's Uniswap v4 pool pays a 0.98% base fee plus the creator's 1-10% tax, in the coin's paired asset (QuoteFeeTaken events of each coin's hook). Swaps in a coin's first 3 seconds also pay an anti-snipe surcharge. The pool's own LP fee is 0.
methodology.Revenue: 20% of every trading fee (the portal's platformBps) plus the whole anti-snipe surcharge go to the Phlece team Safe.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 20% of every trading fee plus the anti-snipe surcharge, paid to the Phlece team Safe.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The other 80% of each trading fee, split by percentages the coin's creator fixed at launch between the creator, the coin's holders (dividends), buyback-and-burn of the coin, and liquidity added to the coin's locked pool position.

Fees.Trading Fees: 0.98% base fee plus the creator's 1-10% tax on every swap, in the paired asset.
Fees.Anti-Snipe Surcharge: Extra charge on swaps in a coin's first 3 seconds (99%, then 6.18%, then 0.19%).

Revenue.Trading Fees To Protocol Treasury: 20% of each trading fee, to the team Safe.
Revenue.Anti-Snipe Surcharge To Protocol Treasur: The whole anti-snipe surcharge, to the team Safe.

ProtocolRevenue.Trading Fees To Protocol Treasury: 20% of each trading fee, to the team Safe.
ProtocolRevenue.Anti-Snipe Surcharge To Protocol Treasur: The whole anti-snipe surcharge, to the team Safe.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: The creator's share of the remaining 80%, claimable by the creator's payout wallet.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees To Launched Token Holders: The dividend share, claimable by the coin's holders pro rata.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees To Launched Token Buyback A: Spent buying the coin back from its pool and sending it to 0xdead.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees To Launched Token Locked Li: Added to the coin's permanently locked pool position.
